title: Fitting random labels
description: Deep networks fit random labels, then perform at chance on test images.

coverage.scope_note: This snapshot contains the saved merged final records used by this entry, including records not individually shown on the page. It is not an exhaustive collection of experiments or papers. Missing records, omitted extraction and not-tested statements are different from negative results.

claims.heading: Deep networks fit random labels without changing architecture or training hyperparameters
Random labels add modest training time, with convergence slowing as corruption increases
Networks can fit permuted pixels and Gaussian noise to zero training error
Networks can fit corrupted labels while test performance degrades
Networks can fit random labels with regularization and generalize without it
Networks often learn real patterns before memorizing noisy labels

related_findings.title: Better supervision improves performance under label noise
related_findings.summary: Selecting examples, correcting labels and changing supervision can improve held-out performance under partial corruption. These gains alone do not establish reduced memorization of corrupted labels.

examples.headline: Co-teaching improves clean-test accuracy over standard CNN training with feature-correlated errors in Te data.
BL+FN, a noisy-label method, improves MNIST clean-test accuracy under heavy corruption; noisy-label fitting is unreported.
WARw2v beats categorical cross-entropy on Fashion-MNIST, CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 under asymmetric label noise.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Corruption changes internal geometry and spectra
related_findings.summary: Label corruption changes the geometry of learned representations, activation statistics, and gradient or weight spectra (how strongly different directions contribute). How these measures relate to memorization and generalization depends on architecture, layer and training stage.

examples.headline: In synthetic networks, label corruption raises effective curvature, weighted parameter size and a proposed generalization-error bound.
Grokking modular-division transformers have lower minimum local dimensionality than models with persistently low validation accuracy.
Corruption raises peak Fisher effective rank, a dimensionality measure; clean and corrupted examples contribute oppositely.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Detecting label errors depends on training conditions
related_findings.summary: Loss, curvature, influence and other diagnostic measures can identify errors in supervision. Their reliability depends on the corruption, example difficulty, learned representation and training stage.

examples.headline: Influential Rank, an influence-based method, detects corrupted CIFAR-10 labels using clean validation examples.
Loss curvature with respect to inputs, averaged across epochs, detects synthetic label errors with weight decay.
In federated learning, loss against labels detects persistent label flips better than each client's uncertainty.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: More corruption can reduce held-out performance
related_findings.summary: Held-out performance often declines as partial label corruption increases over the tested ranges. These results do not establish perfect training fit, strict monotonicity or a chance endpoint.

examples.headline: Cross-entropy test accuracy falls with symmetric CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 corruption; training-label fitting is unreported.
ImageNet-pretrained ResNet50's multi-label UCMerced test mean average precision falls as injected noise increases.
Fashion-MNIST test accuracy with categorical cross-entropy falls as asymmetric label noise increases.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Training changes can reduce corrupted-label fitting
related_findings.summary: Modified objectives, gradient aggregation, example weighting and forgetting procedures can suppress or reverse corrupted-label fitting. Useful learning can persist under these interventions in the reported settings.

examples.headline: SIGUA forgets flipped MNIST labels and improves test accuracy when told exactly which examples are corrupted.
Modified AllConv (IOC-AllConv) fits fully corrupted labels poorly, outperforming standard AllConv under partial corruption.
RMD's training fit and test accuracy vary with lambda under partial CIFAR-10 corruption.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Error structure matters at matched corruption rates
related_findings.summary: The structure of annotation errors changes fitting and held-out performance beyond the overall error rate. Spatially concentrated errors, speech error types and structured image-label errors have different effects from random corruption.

examples.headline: Locally clustered MNIST label errors yield lower overall prediction accuracy than randomly spread errors.
At matched word-level error rates, deletions harm RNN-T performance more than substitutions or insertions.
BiomedCLIP's structured errors lower PCAM test area under the curve more than equally frequent random errors.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Regularization effects depend on the setting
related_findings.summary: Augmentation, weight penalties, dropout and capacity controls change fitting and generalization. Their effects depend on architecture, noise, task and optimization settings.

examples.headline: Weaker diagonal regularization raises neural tangent kernel random-label training accuracy, while test accuracy stays unchanged.
L2 regularization stabilizes ONN test misclassification under Gaussian target noise.
Selected transfer models using DRFit, ridge or Mixup have low training accuracy, with no reported overfitting.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Test performance can decline after an early peak
related_findings.summary: Continued noisy-label training can worsen generalization after an early peak. Stopping rules and robust objectives can limit this deterioration, but test-performance curves alone do not show which examples the model fitted first.

examples.headline: Cross-entropy test accuracy improves, plateaus and then declines under partial label noise.
CE and SuperLoss decline late under CIFAR-100 noise, while DiscrimLoss plateaus.
TLCM's and ASL's test mean average precision falls after early gains; MPVAE approaches a lower plateau.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Similar training fit can hide different generalization
related_findings.summary: Similar or perfect training fit can coexist with different held-out performance and representation quality. Which solution training finds matters, as do architecture, initialization and training history.

examples.headline: Synthetic two-layer ReLU CNN approaches zero training loss and optimal (Bayes) test error despite label corruption.
An algorithm constructed to fit every label scores lower on true CIFAR-10 labels than trained ResNet18.
Label permutation increases PPA reconstruction distance despite nearly perfect ResNet training accuracy.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Fitting speed depends on data and optimization
related_findings.summary: Memorization speed and convergence depend on input geometry, target complexity, capacity, initialization and optimization. Randomness alone does not determine a universal ordering of fitting difficulty.

examples.headline: Adam with sigmoid units fails to converge on flattened XOR in the tested two-unit networks.
Activation choice changes convergence speed in fixed-feature regression; Swish fails to converge within budget.
Tested transformers' random-label memorization time grows roughly exponentially with dataset information per unit of capacity.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Useful features can survive corrupted-label training
related_findings.summary: Useful features and previously learned information can survive noisy-label fitting or random-label retraining. Retention and accessibility depend on the layer, corruption, augmentation and probe.

examples.headline: Training to predict fixed Gaussian targets improves linear-probe accuracy over random initialization.
Random-label training improves true-label probes with augmentation; without it, ResNet18 training degrades CIFAR10 embeddings.
Random-label face unlearning eliminates forgotten-identity test accuracy while retaining compactness and high base retrieval.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Diagnostics reveal more than training accuracy
related_findings.summary: Confidence, margins, stability, agreement and complexity measures provide information about generalization beyond training fit. Their reliability depends on the model, metric and evaluation conditions.

examples.headline: L2NNNs have smaller training and test confidence gaps with random labels than clean labels.
Semantic-versus-random-label EMC advantage correlates negatively with generalization gap in CNNs and MLPs.
Random-label training increases joint-bank feasibility, which correlates weakly with held-out random-label accuracy.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Interpolation constructions require explicit assumptions
related_findings.summary: Networks can be constructed to fit arbitrary labels under specific constraints on their architecture, input geometry and parameters. These guarantees about capacity alone do not show that stochastic gradient training will converge.

examples.headline: Constructed two-layer ReLU networks fit arbitrary labels on inputs in general position, without establishing SGD convergence.
A width-2 network of specified depth fits any nonnegative class labels on distinct inputs.
Required side-network size grows approximately with the square root of changed random targets.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Generalization after interpolation depends on the solution
related_findings.summary: Noisy interpolators can generalize under specific assumptions about the estimator, features, signal and geometry. Other settings retain substantial excess risk despite small training loss.

examples.headline: The ideal Gaussian-feature linear interpolator has an excess-MSE bound under specified dimensional conditions.
Under specified kernel-limit conditions and Gaussian noise, excess risk falls as interpolating solutions grow in norm.
A two-layer network on spherical inputs retains substantial excess risk despite tiny training loss.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Pretraining changes later memorization and transfer
related_findings.summary: Prior training can improve transfer, accelerate later memorization or impair subsequent learning. Outcomes depend on the learned representation, downstream objective and treatment of the encoder.

examples.headline: Random-label cross-pretraining improves downstream validation accuracy on HMDB51 and UCF-101.
Random-label ResNet-20 pretraining gives iteratively magnitude-pruned subnetworks no early benefit; longer pretraining hurts accuracy.
Noisy-pretrained GoogLeNet memorizes an incorrectly relabeled example faster than its clean-pretrained counterpart.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Models and training procedures differ in fitting random labels
related_findings.summary: Arbitrary-target fitting and its generalization cost depend on architecture, effective capacity, data and training procedure. Some tested models fit random labels completely, while others remain far from complete fitting.

examples.headline: Greedily spectrally trained KNet perfectly fits random labels, with the test chance level unspecified.
Spline-only KAN (Kolmogorov-Arnold network) fits random MNIST labels poorly across the reported training budgets.
Under partial label noise, the quantum head loses less peak-to-final test accuracy than the classical head.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Learning favors some functions and examples
related_findings.summary: Learning can favor simpler functions, lower frequencies and easier valid examples. Learning rate, initialization, input geometry and target structure affect these preferences and their generalization consequences.
related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Random labels expose evaluation leakage
related_findings.summary: Randomized-label controls can reveal inflated performance caused by overlapping data or model selection, while some reported validation protocols score near chance.

examples.headline: With randomized subject labels, MRI-slice accuracy stays high when training and evaluation include the same subjects.
With scrambled training labels, DAPPER's validation Matthews correlation coefficient, a classification score, stays near zero.
Nested-CV and untouched external estimates remain near chance under random labels; comparison estimates are higher.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Fitting labels does not establish perturbation robustness
related_findings.summary: Robustness around memorized examples depends on the task and perturbation. Fitting noisy labels can coexist with fragile predictions and poor adversarial robustness.

examples.headline: Shuffled-label training error under small FGSM (fast-gradient-sign) attacks grows as a power law of attack size.
Adversarial training (PGD-AT, TRADES) fails to reach near-perfect robust random-label training accuracy within the tested budget.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Memorization and generalization occur on different timescales
related_findings.summary: When a model memorizes, forgets or generalizes depends on the task, its capacity and initialization, and its kernel geometry. Useful generalization may appear briefly or emerge late.

examples.headline: In the tested modular-addition MLP, label noise delays the generalization jump after reaching a training-accuracy threshold.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Test risk can peak near perfect training fit
related_findings.summary: Test risk can rise near the point where models fit every training label, then decline with additional capacity or training. Later improvement depends on noise, features, regularization and the evaluation metric.

examples.headline: Noisy MNIST-1D test error peaks near perfect training fit, falling as MLP and CNN size increases.
At tested widths and noise, error's dip before interpolation is lower than its dip after interpolation.
At fixed label corruption, test error peaks near perfect training fit, improving as parameter counts increase.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Aggregate performance can miss retained training information
related_findings.summary: Attacks and probes of individual examples can reveal retained training information that overall accuracy or train–test performance gaps miss. These findings depend on the model, data and assumptions about how the attack works.

examples.headline: An attack recovers singleton bits from an MLP despite almost complete fresh-singleton classification failure.
MNIST VAE memorization scores rise before train-test gaps appear; lower learning rates reduce peak scores.
Malicious selective aggregation increases membership-inference attack success, measured by AUC, on MNIST, EUROSAT and PATHMNIST.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Dedicated components can separate memorization from useful learning
related_findings.summary: Dedicated heads, experts, neurons and adapters can route learning from clean labels and memorization of noisy labels into separate components. Changing these components can change model outputs while internal representations persist.

examples.headline: Example-tied dropout ResNet-9 nearly perfectly fits clean and noisy CIFAR-10 subsets before designated neurons are removed.
The tested model reaches near-zero training loss on both real and randomly assigned answers.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Teacher choices and training objectives affect distillation outcomes
related_findings.summary: Teacher selection, temperature, training objective and additional data affect distillation under noisy labels. Teacher outputs can transfer memorized information as well as task patterns that generalize.

examples.headline: Combining teachers trained on noisy labels improves test accuracy; distilling with CIFAR-5m data improves it further.
Small-temperature KL distillation generalizes best under CIFAR-100 noise; MSE does not prevent degradation above 50%.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Memorization can support rare and difficult examples
related_findings.summary: Information specific to rare or difficult valid examples can support generalization. Removing influential examples or correcting their labels can harm the model's learning of those examples.

examples.headline: Removing high-influence CIFAR-100 examples reduces test accuracy, mainly on the test examples they influence.
Self-adaptive label correction reduces minority-class accuracy relative to cross-entropy, especially under stronger imbalance.
Removing SST-2 examples that strongly influence their own predictions harms test accuracy more than random removal.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Noisy examples affect optimization before being fitted
related_findings.summary: Clean and noisy examples shape gradients differently throughout training. Their relative influence depends on training time, architecture, normalization and how the model is adapted.

examples.headline: Clean-to-noisy gradient magnitudes approach parity by early stopping in binary MNIST; corruption descriptions differ.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Random-label training changes agreement between models on unseen inputs
related_findings.summary: Random-label training can change representations and agreement between predictions from separately trained models. Models that agree on fitted training labels need not make similar predictions on unseen inputs.

examples.headline: Random-label models' test-prediction agreement clusters at low and high levels, while test accuracy stays at chance.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Simple shortcuts can harm performance on subgroups and shifted data
related_findings.summary: Simple predictive shortcuts and example-specific nuisance features can obstruct learning of core features. Feature interventions, weighting and optimization can change subgroup and shifted-distribution performance.

examples.headline: Randomizing the simplest predictive feature collapses AUC on constructed datasets; randomizing complex features does not.
Standard models struggle on examples contradicting dataset biases; the LfF method improves performance across groups.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Other model families also fit arbitrary labels
related_findings.summary: Linear classifiers, kernels, Gaussian processes and random forests can fit randomized or partially corrupted targets under suitable capacity and data conditions. Their generalization depends on the model and setting.

examples.headline: Weakly regularized logistic regression memorizes randomized MNIST labels and makes random, overconfident test predictions.
A Gaussian process with an RBF kernel perfectly fits random CIFAR-10 labels despite low test accuracy.
Maximum-margin linear classifiers have unseen-data error bounds under stated assumptions and fit noisy Boolean simulations exactly.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Classifiers on fixed representations test a distinct fitting capacity
related_findings.summary: Classifiers differ in their ability to fit arbitrary labels when the input representations stay fixed. The learned representations and the classifier's capacity make this test distinct from memorization when the whole model is trained.

examples.headline: For tested representation methods, classifier training accuracies correlate across datasets for normal and shuffled labels.
Two-layer MNLI classifiers' validation accuracy varies across bag-of-words, pretrained RoBERTa-large and fine-tuned RoBERTa-large representations.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Classification success does not establish correct class probabilities
related_findings.summary: Predicted probabilities can reflect local or corrupted label distributions. Useful classification under noise alone does not establish recovery of clean-label probabilities or calibration.
related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Random labels change information and compression measurements
related_findings.summary: Label randomization changes estimated weight information and compressibility. The interpretation depends on how information is defined and measured.

examples.headline: Small AlexNet's estimated weight information rises with label corruption under the study's penalty on weight information.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Continued random-data learning depends on plasticity
related_findings.summary: Models can learn additional random data or successive random-label tasks. Their ability to keep learning and retain prior capabilities depends on plasticity—the capacity to adapt—and the training procedure.

examples.headline: Tested models fit combined original and random data nearly perfectly after their vocabulary is enlarged.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Generative models retain training structure in different ways
related_findings.summary: Autoencoder attraction and diffusion score interpolation can retain training-specific structure. Population behavior depends on architecture, initialization, sample size, smoothing and stopping.

examples.headline: An MNIST autoencoder reconstructs well; repeatedly feeding test-image reconstructions back as inputs converges to training examples.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Federated training changes fitting and generalization timing
related_findings.summary: Federated averaging can slow noisy-label fitting. Peak performance and test-accuracy trajectories depend on noise levels and client heterogeneity.

examples.headline: Federated models memorize noisy labels more slowly but may miss centralized training's peak test accuracy.
With noisy labels, federated averaging's test accuracy rises initially and then declines.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Mismatched image-text pairs change alignment and memorization
related_findings.summary: Noisy image-text correspondences change alignment and measured memorization. The training procedure affects how well clean and mismatched pairs separate.

examples.headline: Mis-captioned COCO pairs have higher memorization scores than clean pairs; clean-pair scores stay similar across models.
During training, method SDD increasingly separates clean and mismatched Flickr30K pairs; method NPC's early separation weakens.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Later interventions change memorization and held-out performance
related_findings.summary: Classifier editing, feature projection and targeted continuation can alter memorized information and held-out performance. Outcomes depend on the layer, evaluation data and intervention strength.
related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Memorization can retain irrelevant input details
related_findings.summary: Networks can retain unique or task-irrelevant input features. Architecture, augmentation, training randomness and feature alignment affect this retention, which different memorization measures may capture differently.

examples.headline: Augmentation increases measured unique-feature memorization in a CIFAR-10 CNN; this measure does not assess random-label fitting.

related_findings.relationship_note: Related findings do not necessarily test an existing claim as worded.

related_findings.title: Consistent label inversion can remain learnable
related_findings.summary: Consistently inverting binary labels can preserve a learnable task. Training loss need not increase monotonically with the label-flip rate.

examples.headline: In the HDFS dataset, fully inverted labels yield lower, decreasing training loss than partially flipped labels.

reading_list.why: Establishes the baseline random-label experiments, including training fit, test performance, corruption sweeps and regularizer removal.
Examines learning order under partial corruption and how tuned dropout reduces random-label fitting while preserving clean-data learning.
Pairs perfect training fit with declining test accuracy across corruption rates, including fully random labels.

known_gaps.summary: The main gaps concern matched training conditions, measured fitting times, evidence at larger scales, learning order, source reliability and independent reproduction.
items: Complete random-label fitting under unchanged hyperparameters and training budgets remains unresolved across settings. Some successful fits required longer training, a different learning rate or removal of regularization and augmentation.

How much random labels slow training remains poorly established. Similar loss curves and qualitative reports of slower learning do not establish that fitting takes only a small multiple of the usual training time.

At billion-parameter scale, some results have not been independently reproduced. Qwen3-14B's nearly complete fitting does not establish that every training example was fitted, and its reported fitting on TinyImageNet-200 remains incomplete.

Learning clean examples before corrupted examples is not established across asymmetric, feature-dependent, adversarial and very high noise. Declining held-out performance alone cannot establish the order in which examples are fitted.

Disagreements about augmentation, noise sensitivity and worsening test performance need comparisons with matched training procedures and budgets. An ImageNet run stopped before fitting all training examples, leaving it unknown whether fitting would eventually finish.

Some influential reports of failed or reversed effects remain qualitative or lack final numerical results and uncertainty estimates. For other findings, discrepancies between the reported results and the cited passages remain unresolved.

It is unclear whether some apparently corroborating reports are independent: they include the same publications under different names, overlapping studies and shared authors. These relationships need clarification before judging how broadly findings have been reproduced.
